definitions.explanation: Distinctly different from others in a category; standing out as one of a kind. Used in both neutral-descriptive and scientific contexts to indicate something that deviates notably from the norm.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{特異|とくい}な{才能|さいのう}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}だ。
examples.english: He is a person with a unique talent.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}には{特異|とくい}な{生態系|せいたいけい}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
examples.english: A unique ecosystem spreads across this region.

examples.japanese: {特異|とくい}{体質|たいしつ}のため、この{薬|くすり}を{服用|ふくよう}すると{副作用|ふくさよう}が{出|で}やすい{患者|かんじゃ}もいる。
examples.english: Due to their peculiar constitution, some patients are prone to side effects when taking this medication.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a na-adjective ({特異|とくい}な) to describe people, phenomena, or things that are distinctly different. Common in academic, scientific, and medical contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {特異|とくい}な{才能|さいのう} (unique talent)
- {特異|とくい}{体質|たいしつ} (peculiar constitution)
- {特異|とくい}{点|てん} (singular point — used in mathematics and science)
- {特異|とくい}な{存在|そんざい} (unique existence/being)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {独特|どくとく}: distinctive, characteristic (neutral, emphasizes individuality)
- {特殊|とくしゅ}: special, specialized (implies requiring special handling or expertise)
- {得意|とくい}: good at, skilled in (same reading but different kanji and meaning)
